messages.subject: Re: Is it possible to read in tabix files previously generated?
messages.subject_clean: Is it possible to read in tabix files previously generated?
messages.body_plain:
So basically your request to read tabix files is already included in methylKit. If you use dbtype ="tabix" with the methRead function it internally checks wether this file is already a tabix file and if true, it links the methylRawDB objects to the tabix file.
 But you can not merge compressed and uncompressed files in methRead, so my idea would be to process your remaining (uncompressed) files and afterwards pass all together to the function.

Check the code below to get an idea about reading compressed files:

library(methylKit)

# I have two files, one is already processed, the other not
compr.file.path <- system.file("extdata", "test1.txt.bgz", package = "methylKit")
uncompr.file.path <- system.file("extdata","test1.myCpG.txt",package = "methylKit")

# the compressed can be directly loaded by using the path to the database file
myobj.db <- methRead(location = compr.file.path,sample.id <http://sample.id> = "test1",assembly = "hg18")
# you need to take care of the dbtype parameter ( is NA by default)
myobj.db <- methRead(location = compr.file.path,sample.id <http://sample.id> = "test1",assembly = "hg18",dbtype = "tabix")

# the uncompressed needs to be processed before
myobj2.db <- methRead(location = uncompr.file.path,sample.id <http://sample.id> = "test1",assembly = "hg18",dbtype = "tabix")

# merging uncompressed and compressed files will lead to error
myobj.list.db <- methRead(location = list(compr.file.path,uncompr.file.path),sample.id <http://sample.id> = list("test1","test2"),treatment = c(1,1),assembly = "hg18",dbtype = "tabix")

# you have to process uncompressed files beforehand and can than load them together
myobj2.list.db <- methRead(location = list(compr.file.path,myobj2.db@dbpath),sample.id <http://sample.id> = list("test1","test2"),treatment = c(1,1),assembly = "hg18",dbtype = "tabix")

Best,

Alex

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] regarding threshold number of cytosine in a tiles
messages.subject_clean: [methylkit_discussion] regarding threshold number of cytosine in a tiles
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I don't have structured investigation for this, so don't have a great answer for the cutoff. One can look at tiles that have many cytosines covered, and remove one cytosine at time, to see how the aggregated methylation values are changing and find a lower bound.

This is also related to number of CpGs in the tile, sometimes there will be only one CpG occurring in a tile.

Another strategy is to have cutoff on total coverage of CpGs on a tile and forgetting about number of CpGs.

Best,
Altuna

I want to calculate differential DNA methylation of bovine fat tissues between two groups. I have two samples (cows) of each group and three replicates (three sequencing libraries) of each sample. I used Bismark and got about 60% unique alignment with reference genome (UMD3.1) of all 12 samples and CpG reports were generated by Bismark Extractor. I have converted CpG reports into text format which was required for MethylKit input.

Now I want your guidance for reading the files in MethylKit WHERE as sampleA and sampleB are in first group. SampleC and sampleD are in second group.

Whether the following code will solve my purpose or guide me in this regard how to deal replicates?

file.list= list (

"sampleA_Replicate_1.txt", "sampleA_Replicate_2.txt", "sampleA_Replicate_3.txt",

Thanks ALTUNA, a bit more explanation about the design of WGBS experiment. We have 4 different animals (cows) which are divided into two different groups on the basis of their phenotypes. Group 1 has two different animals and Group 2 has two other different animals. DNA has been extracted from these 4 animals (4 different samples of DNA). Then 3 sequencing libraries of each of these samples were prepared and sequenced.
Group 1  has six samples:-  G1_Cow1_Lib1,   G1_Cow1_Lib2,  G1_Cow1_Lib3,   G1_Cow2_Lib1,   G1_Cow2_Lib2,  G1_Cow2_Lib3.

Now we have total 12 samples and six samples in each group and two different cows in each group and each cow has three sequence libraries (of the same DNA sample).

I want to calculate differential DNA methylation between Group 1 and Group 2 by using methylKit.

1) What is your recommendation now to proceed further?

2) If pool is required then how to pool the replicates for each sample and then use the regular logistic regression based test (e.g. code)?

Thanks.

Naveed Jhamat,
PhD student.

>
> 1) What is your recommendation now to proceed further?
>

 I would do clustering and PCA for the samples and see replicates cluster together and if there are unexpected patterns.

> 2) If pool is required then how to pool the replicates for each sample and then use the regular logistic regression based test (e.g. code)?

You can pool them providing an appropriate treatment vector and pool() function. The treatment vector could be c(3,3,3,2,2,2,1,1,1,0,0,0), after pooling the treatment vector will be converted to c(3,2,1,0). After that you need to reset it to c(1,1,0,0) to be able to differential methylation calculation.
